deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page deals with sums of three squares and ternary decompositions. The next page is unrelated numerical (astronomical/geodetic) reduction. This page is a short, fragmentary setup for computing the mean value (Valor medius) of an arithmetic function that depends only on the prime-power parts of the argument at a finite set of primes. Most of the content is notation. The final formula is not written, so parts of what follows are my reconstruction and are marked as such.

(1) Top line: 'FA − F(A/p)' and below '(p−1)/p ..... 1'.
- Reading (mine): F(A) is a counting function, e.g. the number of integers 1..A.
- Then F(A) − F(A/p) counts the integers up to A that are not divisible by p (strictly, it subtracts the multiples of p). Asymptotically this is A·(p−1)/p.
- So (p−1)/p is the density of integers prime to p, against density 1 for all integers.
- An alternative reading, also consistent: F(A) = Σ_{d|A} φ(d) = A, so F(A) − F(A/p) = A(p−1)/p when p | A.
- Either way, the factor (p−1)/p is the local density at p.

(2) Struck through: 'D = a^α b^β c^γ …'. This is replaced by the sentence 'D hat die Primzahlen a, b, c zu factoren': D is an integer whose prime factors are a, b, c, ….

(3) 'Man setzt A = L a^α b^β c^γ … , wo L durch keine der Zahlen a, b, c theilbar'. This is the factorization A = L·∏ a^{v_a(A)} with gcd(L, D) = 1. In modern terms α = v_a(A), β = v_b(A), γ = v_c(A).

(4) Notation for 'parts' of A:
- (A,a) = a^α, (A,b) = b^β, …
- (A,ab) = a^α b^β, (A,ac) = a^α c^γ, (A,bc) = b^β c^γ
- (A,abc) = a^α b^β c^γ
- In general (A,D) = ∏_{q|D} q^{v_q(A)}, the D-part of A. This is not the gcd; it is the largest divisor of A built only from primes dividing D.
- (A,u) = A: with u standing for the 'universal' modulus (all primes), the u-part of A is A itself.

(5) 'f(1,a), f(2,a), f(3,a), f(4,a) …'. These are values assigned according to the exponent of the prime a, i.e. f evaluated on a, a^2, a^3, … (local data at a).

(6) 'Valor med. = …'. The intended (unwritten) result is the mean value of a function of (A,D). Implicit steps (mine):
- The set of A with v_a(A) = k has natural density (1/a^k)(1 − 1/a) = (a−1)/a^{k+1}. This is where the (p−1)/p of step (1) enters.
- For distinct primes these conditions are independent (CRT), so the density of A with (A,D) = a^α b^β c^γ… equals ∏ (q−1)/q^{e_q+1}.
- Hence for g(A) = G((A,D)), the mean value is lim (1/N) Σ_{A≤N} g(A) = Σ over the possible D-parts of G(a^α b^β …)·∏ (q−1)/q^{e_q+1}.
- If the dependence is multiplicative across primes (G = ∏ f(e_q, q)), this factorizes as ∏_{q|D} Σ_{k≥0} f(k,q)(q−1)/q^{k+1}.

What it serves: this is the standard way to average quantities, like representation numbers by ternary/binary forms or class-number factors, whose dependence on n is through local prime-power data. That fits the three-squares material on the preceding leaf and Gauss's mean-value statements for class numbers (Disq. Arith. art. 301–304).

The remaining text consists of pen trials and names written as calligraphy, not mathematics: 'Lundit(?)', 'Sponagel', 'Hennings', 'A. w. z', 'woraz', ornamental letters.
errors: No mathematical errors can be detected; the page is a notational setup without a completed derivation.
The notation (A,ab) is used without parentheses in places ('A,ab', 'A,abc'). This is only an inconsistency of writing.
(A,D) here means the D-part ∏_{q|D} q^{v_q(A)}, not the gcd(A,D). Gauss's notation must not be read as gcd.
The formula after 'Valor med. =' is left incomplete. Convergence requires f(k,q) to grow slower than q^k (e.g. bounded), which is not stated.

results.what: Density of integers prime to p is (p−1)/p, via counting F(A) − F(A/p)
results.modern_name: local density / natural density of integers coprime to p (sieve of Eratosthenes count)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (φ product), classical; Legendre's sieve counting 1798–1808

results.what: Decomposition A = L·∏ q^{v_q(A)} with gcd(L,D) = 1, and the notion of the D-part (A,D)
results.modern_name: D-part / p-adic valuations, unitary splitting of an integer

results.what: Set-up for the mean value of a function depending only on the prime-power parts (A,q) for q|D; implied formula mean = ∏_q Σ_k f(k,q)(q−1)/q^{k+1}
results.modern_name: mean value of functions depending on local (p-adic) data; Euler-product for mean values (special case of Wintner/Erdős–Wintner type mean-value theorems)
results.usually_credited_to: general theory: Wintner (1944), Erdős–Wintner (1939), Delange; specific averages of class numbers: Gauss (Disq. Arith. 1801, art. 301–304), proofs by Lipschitz/Mertens (1865–1874)

deep.surprise_reason: The page only sets up notation (prime-power parts of A, local densities (p−1)/p) for computing a mean value, and the formula is unfinished. Gauss's interest in mean values of arithmetic quantities (class numbers, representation numbers) is well documented, and the local-density computation is elementary.

checkable.asserts: The densities of integers with v_p(A) = k, k = 0,1,2,…, sum to 1 (here p = 7).
Example mean value: the average of (number of divisors of the 3-part of A) equals p/(p−1) = 3/2.

checkable.sympy: Rational(len([n for n in range(1,60001) if n % 5 != 0]), 60000) == Rational(4,5)
checkable.asserts: F(A) − F(A/p) counts the integers not divisible by p, giving density (p−1)/p (p = 5, A = 60000).

checkable.sympy: abs(sum(Rational(2**(multiplicity(2,n)>=1 and 1 or 0)) for n in range(1,10001))/10000 - Rational(3,2)) < Rational(1,100)
checkable.asserts: Mean of g(A) = 2 if 2|A else 1 is (1/2)·1 + (1/2)·2 = 3/2, consistent with the product-of-local-densities formula.
Illustrates (A,D) as D-part, not gcd: for A = 720, D = 6, (A,D) = 2^4·3^2 = 144.
